newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open firmer as banks recover.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open firmer as banks recover.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Monday after three consecutive weaker sessions.
Bank issues led other stocks higher after the Dow stabilised on Friday.
At 10.25 a.m. (2325 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 11.6 points firmer at 2,328.1.
Stocks opened firmer across the board with resource issues matching industrials despite weaker base and precious metal prices on Friday.
"The fact that the American market held up on Friday has given local investors a lot of relief," said Jim Tredenick, a dealer at Brisbane brokerage Nevitts.
Tredenick said bank stocks were prime selling targets late last week and so had the furthest to recover.
"I think the market will probably end a little higher than its close on Friday," he said. "This time of year it has a tendency to drift off in the afternoon."
National Australia Bank was leading the majors higher while bellwether resource issue BHP was also firmer and the most active stock by value in early trade.
